output.contract_title: SaaS Subscription Agreement with Enterprise Partner 021 LLC

clauses.clause_text: Customer shall pay all undisputed invoice amounts within thirty (30) days of invoice date.
Vendor shall notify Customer in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of any confirmed Data Breach.
Neither party shall limit its liability under this Agreement for any claims whatsoever.
Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon providing thirty (30) days prior written notice.
This Agreement renews on an annual basis unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 30 days prior.

extraction_notes: Document extracted once for downstream policy comparison

mandatory_requirements.description: Aggregate liability cap must not exceed 12 months of total fees paid or payable.
mandatory_requirements.threshold: Liability limited to an amount equal to twelve (12) months of the total fees that have been paid or are payable under the agreement.

mandatory_requirements.description: Customer must have the right to terminate for convenience with no more than 30 days prior written notice.
mandatory_requirements.threshold: Termination notice period limited to a maximum of thirty (30) days prior to the effective termination date.

ambiguities_in_policy.issue: Definition of "total fees paid or payable" is not specified – unclear whether it includes recurring fees, one‑time fees, taxes, or future escalations.
Phrase "no more than 30 days prior written notice" could be interpreted as a maximum notice period or a minimum required notice; clarification needed.

deviations.supporting_evidence: Mapping status is 'conflicting', indicating the clause's liability cap exceeds the policy threshold of twelve (12) months of total fees paid or payable.
deviations.recommended_remediation: Amend clause CLS-0021-LIAB to limit aggregate liability to an amount equal to no more than twelve (12) months of the total fees that have been paid or are payable under the agreement.

risk_findings.ambiguity_description: The term "undisputed invoice amounts" is not defined, leaving ambiguity about what constitutes a dispute and how it is resolved. No consequences for late payment are specified, creating a potential advantage for the Vendor.
"Confirmed Data Breach" is not defined, and the requirement to notify within 24 hours of becoming aware may be operationally impractical without clear criteria for "awareness" and "confirmation".
The clause removes any liability caps for both parties, exposing each side to potentially unlimited financial exposure for any claim, which is atypical and may be commercially untenable.

evidence_notes.note: Clause text specifies payment of "undisputed invoice amounts" within 30 days but does not define "undisputed" nor penalties for late payment, directly supporting the identified ambiguity and one‑sided covenant risk.
Clause requires notification within 24 hours of becoming aware of a "confirmed Data Breach" without defining "confirmed" or "awareness," confirming the vague wording and impractical timeline risk.
Clause states neither party shall limit liability for any claims, creating unlimited liability exposure, which aligns with the critical risk description.
